## Purpose
`ScopedStore` — the single enforced default-deny read/write path for the typed-artifact substrate (artifacts, runs, workspaces, events, capabilities, exec/subagent/wave audit rows). It is the relocated-and-grown successor to a formerly pure ownership-predicate module, so that the owner/workspace boundary is enforced in exactly one place rather than scattered across callers.

## Shape
- `ScopedStore(owner_id, workspace_id, session=None)` — constructed with the caller's principal; `_acquire()` either reuses an injected `Session` or opens/closes its own `SessionLocal()`, letting both the request-scoped endpoint path and the session-less engine/SSE path share the same methods.
- `_scope_with_visibility` / `_scope_owner_ws` — the two default-deny filter shapes: owner+visibility for models with a `visibility` column (`ArtifactRef`), plain owner+workspace for everything else (`WorkflowRun`, `RunEvent`, `RunCapabilities`, etc.).
- Per-table read/write method groups, each following the same pattern (stamp the helper principal on write, scope-filter on read): `ArtifactRef` (`write_ref`/`get_ref`/`list_refs`/`lineage`), `RunEvent` (`append_event`, `read_events`, the optimistic-concurrency `append_event_next_seq`/`append_event_at_or_after` seq allocators), `DeepLinkNonce`, `WorkflowRun` (`get_run`, `set_run_scope`), `Repository`, `McpCredential`, plus the audit tables `gate_events`/`validation_results`/`hook_runs`/`exec_runs`/`subagent_runs`/`wave_runs`.
- `assert_owns` / `assert_repo_owned` / `assert_mcp_cred_owned` — explicit-denial variants that look up a row's TRUE owner via an unscoped read and raise `PermissionError` on mismatch, used where a cross-owner reference must fail loudly rather than resolve to a silent `None`.

## Why this shape
The module docstring is explicit about two constraints driving the design: an import-direction rule (this module may import `app.models.*` but never `app.api.*`, enforced by `lint-imports`, so the engine cannot accidentally reach the web layer) and a "DB is fully sync" premise, so every method opens/reuses a synchronous `Session` inside an `async def` via the same `_acquire()`/`finally: close if owned` idiom throughout.
